Anna — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise post-call recap and immediate next steps. I've attached our recent eval report and a CSV with the prompt sets we recommend for checkout, returns, and product Q&A.

Recap / recommended models:
- Recommendation A (low-latency, cost-conscious): redwood-mini-quant-v2 — strong on throughput, good for short-turn checkout prompts.
- Recommendation B (higher-quality for long answers / context): redwood-xxl-utf8 — better hallucination control on longer conversations and richer slot-filling.
- Fallback path: redwood-xxl-8bit (compat) if capacity constraints or to reduce cost for non-critical routes.

Multilingual & locale notes (quick):
- EU languages (de, fr, nl): redwood-xxl-utf8 shows best overall quality; we observed occasional declines on Dutch NER in an internal benchmark from May — we include a targeted prompt-set to mitigate.
- Japanese/Korean: redwood-xxl-utf8 and redwood-jp-tuned (experiment) — redwood-jp-tuned has stronger tokenization alignment for JP markets; recommend pilot A/B to validate.

Attachments included: 1) redwood-model-eval-report-20260710.pdf (benchmarks across EU/APAC languages) 2) prompt-set-eu-apac.csv (recommended prompt templates and evaluation prompts) 3) multilingual-benchmarks-2026-links.txt (drive links + sample results).

Suggested next steps:
1) Pilot scope: 2-week eval using our Dedicated trial on 1 GPU with redwood-xxl-utf8 for product Q&A and redwood-mini-quant-v2 for checkout flows.
2) Provide us with a 500–1k prompt sample from your EU/JP traffic (anonymized). We can run quality regressions and return token-level cost/latency estimates.
3) Security/compliance: Naomi will follow up with data residency and SOC2 evidence.

I'll be on PTO Monday but Ethan will field questions and coordinate the pilot kickoff.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
